summary: The Lake Commonwealth: five lake towns with an elected Speaker, friendly to Furvior, suspicious of kings and careful with the temples' loans.

speakers_hall.name: The Speaker's Hall
speakers_hall.desc: The Speaker sits in a hall of pale timber on the lake front, and the town delegates sit on benches below. Debate is long, loud and usually settled by supper.

charter_of_mora.name: The Charter of Mora
charter_of_mora.desc: The charter is carved on a stone slab at the lake front and read aloud each spring. Any townsman may stand beside it and ask the Speaker a question.

lake_fisheries.name: Fisheries of the Lake
lake_fisheries.desc: Boat-guilds fish the lake with long nets and sell the catch fresh on the quays. A good season is measured in barrels and a bad one in complaints.

free_lake.name: The Free Lake
free_lake.desc: The lake is open water, and no king may close it. Boats of every flag drop anchor here and are charged the same dues.

open_ledgers.name: Open Ledgers
open_ledgers.desc: The council has set a clerk to read every loan that comes into the towns, and every clerk is a little suspicious. A lender who has something to hide soon finds the lake unwelcoming.

lake_asks_for_a_shield.title: The Lake Commonwealth Asks for a Shield
lake_asks_for_a_shield.desc: A deputation from Mora arrives at Furvior with a fine speech, a sealed petition and a plain request: a guarantee of the lake's freedom. The riders are needed elsewhere, and the court knows it.

an_honest_inquiry.title: An Honest Inquiry
an_honest_inquiry.desc: The council's clerks have read the temples' loan books line by line. The loans are too generous and the lenders too well informed, and nobody on the council can say why. The Speaker asks what the council should do with the report.

options.name: Keep the findings in the council's chest

focuses.name: The Lake Commonwealth
focuses.desc: Five lake towns choose a Speaker and a council of boat-guilds and wharf-masters. Moira Eraver presides, and the whole commonwealth is proud of its elections and wary of kings.

focuses.name: The Speaker's Hall
focuses.desc: The Speaker's hall is a long timber house with open doors, where any townsman may come in to hear the debate. The council argues in front of the people, and is better for it.

focuses.name: The Guilds of the Lake
focuses.desc: Boat-guilds, rope-walks and wharf-masters meet in their own hall and send delegates to the council. Their coin keeps the commonwealth afloat and their votes keep it honest.

focuses.name: Free Elections of Mora
focuses.desc: Every household in the towns has a voice in choosing the Speaker, and the elections are held with painted tokens in open boats. The losers sail home and the winners buy the ale.

focuses.name: The First Townsmen
focuses.desc: A small circle of old families takes the first seats in the council by right of wealth. The commonwealth is steadier for it, and a little less free.

focuses.name: The Charter of Mora
focuses.desc: The charter is cut on a slab at the lake front, so that every boatman can read what the council may and may not do. Kings have asked to see it, and have gone away thoughtful.

focuses.name: The Lake Towns
focuses.desc: Five towns ring the lake, each with a quay, a market and a guild-hall. The council builds a common workshop on the busiest shore.

focuses.name: Fisheries of the Lake
focuses.desc: Boats go out at dawn from every town, and nets are hung to dry along the shore. The catch is salted, smoked or sold fresh, and nothing is wasted.

focuses.name: The Lake Road Wharves
focuses.desc: Caravans from Furvior reach the lake at Mora's wharves and trans-ship to boats for the northern towns. The wharves are long, and their ledgers are longer.

focuses.name: Boatwrights of Mora
focuses.desc: Boatwrights build lake barges and fast cutters on the north shore, and the yard bell is heard across the water. Every boat carries the guild mark.

focuses.name: The Lake Schools
focuses.desc: Clerks, surveyors and ship-masters learn their trades in the schools on the quays. The tuition is paid by the guilds, and nobody is turned away for lack of coin.

focuses.name: The Richest Lake in the East
focuses.desc: The lake's towns are the richest per head in the East, and the council knows it. Merchants quote Mora's prices as a measure of every other market.

focuses.name: A Commonwealth Among Kings
focuses.desc: Mora is the only council commonwealth among the crowns of the East, and its neighbours treat it as a curiosity. The Speaker asks the council how a commonwealth should behave among kings.

focuses.name: Friendship With Ostoroth
focuses.desc: The highland king's riders come down to the lake each spring, and a pact of neighbours is spoken of. The council debates it for a month and signs it in a day.

focuses.name: The Noris Embassy
focuses.desc: An embassy is sent to Furvior with gifts of lake-pearls and a respectful letter. The riders are told that Mora likes their coin more than their spears.

focuses.name: Neutral Waters
focuses.desc: The lake is declared neutral, and its boats may carry any flag. Both great roads are welcome and neither is trusted.

focuses.name: A Shield for the Lake
focuses.desc: The lake is small and the towns are many, and a host marching along the shore could take them one by one. The council writes to Furvior for a guarantee.

focuses.name: The Free Lake
focuses.desc: The lake is free, and the council has said so in a charter that every harbour has copied. Whatever else the East may become, Mora's water will stay open.

focuses.name: The Council's Question
focuses.desc: The council asks, in open session, why the temples lend so freely and ask so little. Nobody has a good answer, which is itself an answer.

effects.tooltip: The council asks why the temples lend so freely.

focuses.name: Ledgers of the Temples
focuses.desc: The council demands to read the temples' ledgers, and the temples, gently, agree. Every loan is copied by two clerks and checked against the lake's own books.

focuses.name: The Temples' Charity
focuses.desc: The temples open kitchens in every lake town, and no poor man goes hungry. The council accepts the gift with thanks and does not ask what it costs.

focuses.name: An Honest Inquiry
focuses.desc: A committee of clerks, boatmen and two elders is chosen by lot to inquire into the temples' loans. They are told to find the truth and to say only what they can prove.

focuses.name: Close the Houses of Mora
focuses.desc: The council votes to shut the houses that have lent so freely and asked so little, and the doors are closed in a single morning. The lake's debts are honoured, and its trust is a little less easily given.
